EXTRA CLASS · ANIMAL CATEGORIES

Every animal family, with its lesson on the card.

The sorting class: twenty-three animal families walk the deck in tour order — the friends at home and on the farm, the little crawly creatures, the feathered, finned and scaly teams, the big wild ones, four full habitats, and the giants and old wonders — and every lesson below is a kid-followable guide, right on this page.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Every animal family — with a lesson on its card.

The Animal Categories class is a bonus class, kept beside the main learning path like the Kitchen Helper and the Doctor Visit: the regular classes stay the core sequence, and this one is for the days when somebody asks what kind of animal is that? Twenty-three animal families — the pets on the sofa, the crew in the barn, the bugs in the garden, the giants of the savanna — each one on its own spotter card with four labeled animals, and each card opens a simple lesson a kid can follow: what the family is, who belongs to it, and one way to play it at home tonight.

The families run in tour order on purpose. The deck starts with the animals your child already loves — pets, then the farm — and walks outward: the crawly crew, the feathered and scaly teams, the big wild ones, four full habitats, and the finale of giants and old wonders. By the end, ninety-two labeled animals sit in one deck, sorted and named — and the most requested family of all, the dinosaurs, moved next door into a class of their own with thirty-three cards, one per dinosaur.

Twenty-three cards, six kinds of families.

Twenty-three animal families in six groups, in the order a young naturalist meets them. Every lesson is right here on this page — the original card beside the kid-followable guide, family after family.

THE CLASS GAME

The Big Sort: put the whole zoo in order.

Lay all the cards face up on the floor. Now sort the whole zoo into teams — fur, feathers, scales, shells — calling each animal to its team out loud: the dolphin is a breath-air mammal! The frog lives two lives! The crab walks sideways! Count each team when the sort is done, then sort again tomorrow by size, or by where they live, or by who eats grass. The deck reshuffles itself into a new science lesson every single time — and the losing team gets to hide and be found, which is the part everybody waits for.

SAME ANIMAL, TWO NAMES

Ladybug and ladybird. Both are right.

Animals carry their names across oceans like passports. This class says so out loud. The ladybug is the ladybird in Britain — same little red beetle with the black spots. The cougar goes by three names: cougar, puma and mountain lion — one cat, all correct. The rabbit is everybody’s bunny when it is being adorable. Whichever your family says, your child hears both — and learns early that animals, like words, come in families.

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. The age pill on every card is an honest hint, not a rule: start with the animals your child already loves, follow the questions, follow the child. The familiar families ride Ages 3+, the habitat and concept families ride Ages 4–5 — and any card a child loves is the right card today.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 23 cards in Animal Categories, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Animal Categories. We have 23 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Pets

    “Pets! These are the animals that live at home with us. Dogs wag their tails, cats purr, rabbits hop, and hamsters run on their wheel all night. We feed them, we are gentle with them, and they are our friends.”

    How: Play pet shop with the stuffed animals: one shopkeeper, one customer, and every pet needs a name, a favorite food and a home box. Being gentle is the rule of the whole game.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Farm Animals

    “Farm animals! The cow says moo and gives us milk, the pig says oink, the sheep says baa and gives us wool, and the horse says neigh and gives us rides. The farm is a whole team of helpers!”

    How: Old MacDonald with actions: one corner of the room is the barn, and every animal card sends a different animal walk — stomp like a horse, wiggle like a pig, nibble like a sheep. Sounds on, of course.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · More Farm Animals

    “More farm animals! The goat climbs, the donkey sings hee-haw, the alpaca wears fluffy wool like a sweater, and the buffalo is big and strong. Every barn has more friends than you think!”

    How: Farm-charades: act one animal at a time — climb like a goat, carry a cushion like a donkey, fluff like an alpaca, stomp like a buffalo — and the family guesses. The hee-haw always gives it away.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Farm Birds

    “Farm birds! The chicken says cluck and lays eggs, the duck says quack and swims, the turkey struts — gobble gobble — and the goose honks louder than the tractor! Feathers and beaks everywhere.”

    How: Egg-carton march: line up four toy birds or paper cups as chicken, duck, turkey and goose, and walk each one its own walk — waddle, strut, paddle, honk. Feathers optional, noise not.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Insects

    “Insects! Six legs, little bodies, big jobs. The butterfly flies from flower to flower, the bee makes honey, the ladybug — some say ladybird — eats the bugs that bother plants, and the dragonfly zips over the pond like a tiny helicopter.”

    How: Bug walk: in the garden or the park, hunt for the four card insects with your eyes only — no touching needed. Count wings, count legs, and give every found bug a name of its own.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Garden Creatures

    “Garden creatures! The snail carries its home on its back, the earthworm wiggles underground and helps the plants grow, the caterpillar munches leaves — munch, munch — and the grasshopper jumps! Jump, jump, jump!”

    How: After the rain, go on a slow-creature hunt: snails and worms come out when the ground is wet. Watch how the snail leaves a shiny trail, then put every creature back where you found it.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Small Animals

    “Small animals! The mouse is quick and quiet, the guinea pig squeaks wheek-wheek when it wants a snack, the mole digs tunnels under the grass, and the beaver builds houses out of sticks in the river. Small bodies, big work!”

    How: Small-animal obstacle course: crawl like a mouse, dig like a mole under a blanket, stack blocks like a beaver building a dam, and squeak like a guinea pig at the finish line.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Amphibians

    “Amphibians! They live in water AND on land — two homes, one animal. The frog hops and sings ribbit, the toad walks and warts, the salamander and the newt have tails and like the rain. Damp skin, big adventures!”

    How: Play the frog life cycle: crouch small as an egg, wiggle as a tadpole, sprout arms and legs, then HOP around the room as a frog. The metamorphosis dance is the lesson, and it ends in jumping.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Birds

    “Birds! Feathers, beaks, two wings, two legs. The parrot copies your words, the penguin waddles and swims, the owl says who-who in the dark, and the flamingo stands on one leg — try it! One leg is harder than it looks.”

    How: Bird Olympics: stand on one leg like a flamingo (count to five), waddle like a penguin across the room, turn your head slowly like an owl, and repeat one word three times like a parrot. Award a feather for each event.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Fish

    “Fish! They swim, they have fins and they breathe water — real water-breathers. The salmon swims upstream to where it was born, the goldfish swims in circles at home, the piranha has tiny sharp teeth, and the catfish has whiskers like a cat!”

    How: Fish-y yoga: lie on your back, arms and legs up, and wiggle everything — the goldfish wiggle. Then fold your hands into a fin and glide around the room. Bubble sounds required.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Sea Creatures

    “Sea creatures! The seahorse swims standing up, the starfish has arms and no face you can point to, the crab walks sideways — side, side, side — and the jellyfish floats like jelly. The ocean is full of surprises!”

    How: Ocean-movement game: scuttle sideways like a crab, float slowly like a jellyfish with arms dangling, balance on one spot like a seahorse holding seagrass, and stretch five arms like a starfish.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Reptiles

    “Reptiles! Scales and sunshine. The snake slithers — ssss — with zero legs, the crocodile snaps its big jaw, the chameleon changes its color to match the day, and the lizard does push-ups on a warm rock.”

    How: Reptile charades: slither flat like a snake, chomp slow-motion like a crocodile, change your "color" by walking to different-colored cushions, and do three lizard push-ups on the rug.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Big Animals

    “Big animals! The zebra wears stripes — no two zebras have the same stripes, like fingerprints! The rhino has a horn on its nose, the hippo loves the water and opens its mouth WIDE, and the gorilla beats its chest — boom, boom!”

    How: Big-animal measuring: lie down next to the sofa and ask "which big animal am I longer or shorter than?" Stripes made of painter’s tape on a t-shirt make an instant zebra.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Safari Animals

    “Safari animals! The lion is the king — ROAR — the elephant sprays water with its trunk, the giraffe eats leaves from the tops of the trees, and the monkey swings, swings, swings. Ready for the safari jeep?”

    How: Safari drive: chairs in a row become the jeep, someone drives, and each animal card appears at a "window" — walk like an elephant with an arm-trunk, stretch high like a giraffe, prowl like a lion. Binoculars from toilet rolls complete the trip.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Wild Cats

    “Wild cats! The tiger is the biggest cat in the world — stripes, stripes, stripes. The leopard can climb trees carrying its dinner, the cougar purrs like a giant house cat, and the lynx has furry ears with little paintbrush tips!”

    How: Quiet-paws game: walk from couch to kitchen without making a single sound — cats land soft. Then one giant leap like a tiger, and a tree-climbing stretch like a leopard. Purring optional but encouraged.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Primates

    “Primates! Our cousins with clever hands. The chimpanzee uses a stick to fish for termites, the orangutan hangs by its long arms, the baboon lives in big noisy troops, and the lemur waves its black-and-white ringed tail!”

    How: Hand-skill minute: primates are famous for clever fingers — stack five small blocks, thread three big buttons on a string, turn three pages one at a time. Clever hands are the family superpower.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Forest Animals

    “Forest animals! The bear sleeps all winter — a very long nap! The fox has a white tail tip, the deer walks on quiet hooves, and the squirrel buries acorns — and remembers where, mostly!”

    How: Acorn hide-and-seek: hide five "acorns" (pebbles, balls of paper) around the room, then take turns being the squirrel who hunts them. The bear’s job is to sleep through the whole thing on the couch.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Desert Animals

    “Desert animals! The camel walks across the sand for days, the meerkat stands up tall to look for danger, the scorpion hides under rocks with its curly tail, and the fennec fox has the biggest ears in the desert!”

    How: Meerkat watch: one child stands on a cushion as the lookout while the others dig (in a sandpit or rice bin). Swap guards every ten seconds — real meerkat groups take turns on duty all day.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Arctic Animals

    “Arctic animals! It is cold, cold, cold — but not for them! The polar bear swims in icy water, the seal slides on its belly, the penguin waddles in its tuxedo, and the walrus has two big tusks for pulling out of the water. Brrr? Not for these friends!”

    How: Blubber experiment: put one hand in a bag of ice — brrr! Then put the same hand inside a second bag full of shortening (a "blubber glove") dipped in the ice, and feel how warm seals and penguins stay. Science, with wows.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Australian Animals

    “Australian animals! The kangaroo hops — boing, boing — with a baby in its pouch, the koala naps in the tree all day, the wombat digs long tunnels, and the platypus has a duck’s bill and lays eggs! Australia is full of one-of-a-kind friends.”

    How: Kangaroo relay: jump from cushion to cushion with a stuffed toy tucked into a "pouch" (apron pocket, hoodie pouch). Dropping the joey sends you back one rock — Australia is big, take your time.

  24. Cards 21–23
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Whales & Dolphins

    “Whales and dolphins! The whale is bigger than a bus and sings songs across the whole ocean, the dolphin jumps and whistles hello, and the manatee and dugong are the sea’s gentle cows — they munch seagrass all day, slowly, slowly.”

    How: Whale-song phones: two paper cups joined by string, one person hums a long whale song, the other listens and answers. Then jump like a dolphin between the waves (two cushions) and float like a manatee on the rug.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Night Animals

    “Night animals! While you sleep, they wake up. The bat flies in the dark using echoes — like shouting and listening for the bounce! The raccoon washes its food with clever fingers, the hedgehog curls into a ball, and the firefly blinks — blink, blink — to say good evening.”

    How: Flashlight fireflies: dim the lamps, give everyone a torch, and blink slow signals across the room — fireflies talk in blinks. Then wrap in a blanket and roll gently like a hedgehog ball (on a soft rug, one roll at a time).

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Rainforest Animals

    “Rainforest animals! The parrot squawks in rainbow colors, the toucan has a beak as big as its body, the sloth moves in slow motion — slowwww — and the tree frog climbs the leaves with sticky toes. The rainforest is loud, green and full of life!”

    How: Sloth speed race: the slowest animal wins! Crawl from chair to couch as slowly as possible without stopping — the last one to finish is the champion sloth. Then burst into five fast frog jumps to feel the difference.

  28. 25
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  29. 26
    Check

    “Can you find Pets? Now show me Reptiles.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  30. 27
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 23 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
